To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DNA adducts and DNA repair are important biomarkers for cancer risk.
the levels of carcinogen DNA adducts are associated with risk of breast cancer and that DNA repair genotype and phenotype are associated with risk.
DNA adduct levels, measured by ELISA and immunocytochemistry, correlate with exposure to carcinogens, and that DNA repair genotype/ phenotype influence adduct levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and applying methods to determine DNA adducts and DNA repair capacity as a means of understanding the etiology of cancer.

the development of sensitive methods for the determination of carcinogen-Dna adducts and the application of these methods to studies of the role of gene-environment interactions, particularly those involving DNA repair, in the development of human cancer.
identifying and characterizing the molecular and biochemical mechanisms of human cancer, with a focus on breast cancer, using a combination of epidemiologic, molecular and cellular biology methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DNA adducts are a useful biomarker for environmental exposure and DNA repair capacity is an important factor in the development of cancer.
DNA adduct levels in human tissues are associated with risk of cancer development.
DNA adducts are a useful biomarker of exposure to carcinogens and that DNA repair genotype and phenotype can modify the risk associated with exposure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNA adducts are useful biomarkers in breast cancer and that DNA repair genotypes and phenotypes are useful in predicting risk for breast cancer development.

there is a strong association between DNA adduct levels and breast cancer, that DNA repair capacity influences this relationship and, most importantly, that DNA adducts and DNA repair capacity are independent risk factors for breast cancer.
DNA adducts are a useful biomarker of exposure to environmental carcinogens and DNA repair capacity is an important determinant of cancer risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to develop and utilize biomarkers that reflect the interplay of exposure, susceptibility and cancer risk.
DNA repair capacity and adduct levels are important in cancer risk.
DNA repair genotype/ phenotype can modify risk of breast cancer in the presence of exposure to carcinogens.
